Fort Worth Regional Distribution Center

A Risk Management Plan has been implemented at the Fort Worth facility for the prevention of accidental releases of hazardous materials. The facility is located at 850 Transport Drive in Fort Worth (Tarrant County) Texas. The facility is a storage and distribution warehouse that manages various consumer and professional products that are manufactured by S.C. Johnson & Son, Inc. (SCJ) that include (in part) aerosol cans. SC Johnson is a privately held, family-managed company, with worldwide headquarters located in Racine, Wisconsin.                                                                                                                                                                         

Propellants comprised of flammable mixtures subject to federal RMP regulations are in select aerosol-based products stored and managed in association with the Fort Worth RDC. Products stored inside the warehouse ("INTERIOR STORAGE") include Level 2 & 3 aerosols that are stored in a designated aerosol areas (e.g., cages), while Level 1 aerosols may be stored throughout the warehouse. 

In the course of reviewing this RMP in September 2025, it was determined that an update was appropriate to reflect the potential supplemental storage of aerosol products (e.g., Level 1, 2, and/or 3) may be stored outside the building ("EXTERIOR STORAGE") in up to twelve (12) shipping containers that can each contain up to 60 pallets of such products.  When present, a shipping container is positioned along the west exterior wall of the warehouse such that the easternmost end of a shipping container (assuming no longer than a 53' semi-trailer) abuts the wall and its longest side is directed to the west.

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) propellant used in select aerosol products contains several components that are classified as flammable materials under federal RMP regulations. Specifically, the propellants consist of blends of propane (CAS No. 74-98-6),

butane (CAS No. 106-97-8) and isobutane (CAS No. 75-28-5). These are collectively regulated as a flammable mixture. The maximum projected quantities of aerosol products stored at the facility and product propellant weights were used to estimate maximum quantities of RMP-regulated chemicals in the warehouse storage & handling processes. Although the size of each individual aerosol container is relatively small (typically 15 to 17.5 ounce cans), the number of such containers present onsite at any given time has the potential to exceed the corresponding 10,000 pound TQ. The flammable mixture mass reported in Sec. 1.17.c (17,967,450 lbs) is the total of the reportable flammable chemicals, while the total mass of the entire mixture is calculated at 20,567,282 lbs.

The worst case scenario performed, based on EPA's Offsite Consequence Analysis Guidance, indicates that the distance to the 1 psi overpressure endpoint will not extend beyond plant property. No offsite receptors are impacted. There have also been no prior accidents at the facility resulting in any offsite environmental impacts.

Emergency response activities at the Fort Worth Facility are coordinated with the Tarrant County LEPC and the Tarrant County Sheriff Department.

The maximum number of pallets storing flammable mixture-containing products was refined in the course of preparing the 5-year resubmission in 2021, to reflect the best available information at such time.  Such refinements to historic information include:

1. The number of pallets of aerosol products remained the same at 9,200 pallets; however, the relative distribution for use with Level 1 vs. Level 2/3 aerosols was refined, as discussed below.

2. The number of cases per pallet was increased from 110 to 205 cases per pallet, as a worst-case; however, the actual number of cases per pallet generally varies by product depending on packaging & transportations requirements.

3. The number of cans per case (i.e., 12 cans/case) remained the same.
